Bridge Rules

Contract bridge for four players in two partnerships, as played here: you are South, your partner is North.

The rules

Cards and deal
52 cards, 13 for each player. North and South play together against East and West. The dealer calls first, then it goes clockwise.
Auction
In turn each player bids, passes ("no bid"), doubles or redoubles. A bid names a number of tricks over six (1 to 7) and a trump suit or no trump. It must be higher than the last bid: a higher number, or the same number in a higher strain (clubs, diamonds, hearts, spades, no trump). Three passes after a bid end the auction; if all four pass, the same dealer deals again.
Double and redouble
You may double the opponents' last bid; they may then redouble. That raises the score for making or failing the contract.
Contract
The last bid is the contract. The declarer is the player of that side who first named its strain.
Play
The player on the declarer's left leads the first card. Follow suit if you can, otherwise play any card. The highest trump wins the trick, otherwise the highest card of the suit led. The winner leads next.
Dummy
After the opening lead the declarer's partner lays the cards face up and takes no part: the declarer plays them. If North is declarer here, the computer plays; you watch and tap Next after each trick.
Contract points
For each trick over six bid and made: clubs and diamonds 20, hearts and spades 30, no trump 40 for the first and 30 for each further one. Doubled twice as much, redoubled four times. 100 contract points make a game.
Overtricks and undertricks
Overtricks count like contract points; doubled 100 (vulnerable 200), redoubled twice that. For each trick short the opponents get 50 (vulnerable 100); doubled 100, 200, 200, then 300 each (vulnerable 200, then 300 each); redoubled twice that.
Bonuses
Small slam (12 tricks) 500, vulnerable 750; grand slam (13 tricks) 1000, vulnerable 1500. A doubled contract made 50, redoubled 100. Honours: four of the five top trumps in one hand 100, all five or all four aces in no trump 150.
Chicago
Four deals. In the first nobody is vulnerable, in the second and third the dealer's side, in the fourth both. A game brings 300, vulnerable 500. A part-score on the fourth deal brings 100. Part-scores add up to a game; after a game both sides start again from 0.
Rubber
A side is vulnerable once it has won a game. The first side with two games wins the rubber: 700 if the opponents have no game, 500 if they have one.
How the computers bid
A simple natural system (Standard American with five-card majors). Count high-card points: ace 4, king 3, queen 2, jack 1. Open with 12 or more: 1NT with 15-17 and an even hand, 2NT with 20-21, otherwise one of a major with five cards or one of the better minor. With three cards in partner's major raise: 6-9 points to two, 10-12 to three, 13 or more to game. About 26 points together are enough for a game, 33 for a small slam.
PaperGames rules
In rubber bridge, too, a passed-out deal is dealt again by the same dealer. The computers use no conventions such as Stayman or Blackwood.

Example

Bidding 1♥ – 2♥ – 4♥: North opens one heart (12-21 points, five hearts), South raises to two hearts (6-9 points, three hearts), North bids game. Four hearts made: 120 contract points and 300 for the game (not vulnerable) = 420.
